comparator.name: African Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 programme-specific OER was read again through the current official regulatory index on 13 November 2026. Article 2.2 defines no formal specialisations; catalogue history/anthropology, literature/film and linguistics are academic directions. Appendix F distinguishes the new programme for entrants from 2026–2027 from outgoing cohorts. The named new requirements total 60 EC in year 1, 55 EC in year 2 and 60 EC in year 3: 20 components and 175 EC. A further compulsory year-2 position remains T.B.A., 5 EC, level 200. Genuine year-3 discretionary space is 30 EC; it cannot absorb the unnamed requirement. New year-2 Swahili III is 5 EC; outgoing year-2 Swahili II is 10 EC and has a resit provision. The latter cannot replace new Swahili III plus the missing 5 EC. Both Anthropological Linguistics and African Religions and Philosophies are required 5-EC new-programme components; the outgoing choice group is not imported. The compulsory thesis seminar carries 0 EC separately from the 10-EC thesis. Article 4.2 requires Swahili I before II, I and II before III, propaedeutic completion before Study in Africa, and propaedeutic completion plus Study in Africa before the thesis. Current programme and module APIs were retrieved successfully with current imports, but still mix outgoing membership with the new curriculum and supply no explicit name or cohort-applicable correspondence for the T.B.A. component. The current official index and programme-structure page supplied no inspected amendment identifying it. Direct HTTP website requests returned Access Blocked HTML, including at the PDF URL; their HTTP 200 responses are not validated document content. Actual official regulation and page content was available through web retrieval. This confirms the inspected academic facts without claiming a fresh raw-PDF byte comparison. Historical retrieval hashes remain historical. No complete external pathway, UCR feasibility judgment, final comparison or no-match is inferred.

exception.reason: The current adopted revised programme leaves a required 5-EC second-year component unnamed as T.B.A. The supported named subset totals 175 EC. Its identity and applicable academic conditions require an authoritative amendment or explicit cohort-applicable clarification. The current official index, programme-structure page and catalogue do not supply that clarification in the inspected material. No complete 180-EC pathway, final UCR comparison or no-match is approved.
exception.curriculumContext: The adopted new-programme Appendix F supports 20 named components totalling 175 EC: 60 in year 1, 55 in year 2 and 60 in year 3, including 30 EC of genuine elective space and a 10-EC thesis. There are no formal specialisations. A required year-2 T.B.A. component, 5 EC at level 200, remains unnamed. The noncredit thesis seminar is a separate obligation. New Swahili III is counted once in year 2; outgoing Swahili II and the old third-year choice group do not define the new entrant pathway. Article 4.2 progression conditions remain applicable.

audience.programmeDescription: African Studies at Leiden examines African histories, societies, languages, literature and arts, and Africa’s connections with the wider world. Students learn Swahili, develop research skills and spend a study period in Africa. The final year includes elective space and an independent thesis. Disciplinary themes are not separate formal specialisations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is not yet available because a required 5-EC component in Leiden’s revised curriculum has not been identified. This is a limit in the available curriculum evidence, not a conclusion that UCR offers no suitable study possibilities.
